powers.name: Move
powers.description: Move up to your Movement, hex by hex, paying each hex's terrain cost. Provokes attacks of opportunity normally.
powers.source: Universal. Every hero has this and Sidestep from the start.

powers.name: Sidestep
powers.description: Move exactly 1 hex in any direction. It provokes nothing, and the destination’s terrain cost is irrelevant — step into a hex costing 1, 2 or 3 alike. Costs no Stamina, and it is usable every other Turn. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat. Paladins only.
powers.intent: The free half-step, and the drawback is the wait. On the Turn it is down you can be pinned, which is the whole reason it has a cooldown.
powers.source: 2026-08-17. Universal — every hero starts with Move and Sidestep. | 2026-08-17: enemies have it too. This is the rule that makes zones of control soft. | 2026-08-21: Sidestep gets a cooldown of 1 — "it does break this statement of 'it's always available.' No, it's available every other turn." Enemies lose it entirely (engine/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-21: an enemy carries exactly ONE movement power in its data row). Split into two: Sidestep is free but every other Turn; Side Roll costs 1 Stamina but is always there. Rogues and Rangers take Side Roll by default, everyone else Sidestep. Beasts and Civilians get NEITHER. | 2026-08-21: "Leap. It'll move you two squares with no attacks of opportunity given. Cost 2 stamina. And give you +2 Strength until the end of your activation. And this one goes on a Warrior. And let's remove the one we gave to Priest and Mage, they both don't get one." Sidestep narrows to the Paladin — the Warrior took Leap instead, and Mage and Priest now get nothing. | 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation — you pick Move, a Flight, or your bonus move, never two. "Only the full movement actions and things like them benefit from the Move stat, so all of these bonus moves do not benefit from the Move stat."

powers.name: Side Roll
powers.description: Move exactly 1 hex in any direction. It provokes nothing, and the destination’s terrain cost is irrelevant — step into a hex costing 1, 2 or 3 alike. It costs 1 Stamina, and there is no cooldown — you can do it every Turn. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat. Rogues and Rangers.
powers.intent: The same half-step, priced the other way round. Sidestep is free but makes you wait; Side Roll is always there and you pay for it. A Rogue who wants out every single Turn can have it, at a Stamina a Turn.
powers.source: 2026-08-21: Sidestep gets a cooldown of 1 — "it does break this statement of 'it's always available.' No, it's available every other turn." Enemies lose it entirely (engine/DECISIONS.md 2026-08-21: an enemy carries exactly ONE movement power in its data row). Split into two: Sidestep is free but every other Turn; Side Roll costs 1 Stamina but is always there. Rogues and Rangers take Side Roll by default, everyone else Sidestep. Beasts and Civilians get NEITHER. | 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation — you pick Move, a Flight, or your bonus move, never two. "Only the full movement actions and things like them benefit from the Move stat, so all of these bonus moves do not benefit from the Move stat."

powers.name: Leap
powers.description: Move exactly 2 hexes in any direction. It provokes nothing, and the destination’s terrain cost is irrelevant. You gain +2 Strength until the end of the Turn. It costs 2 Stamina and there is no cooldown. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat. Warriors only.
powers.intent: The only movement power that is an opening rather than an escape. Two hexes gets you INTO the fight and the Strength lands on the swing you take when you arrive. It rides your attacks of opportunity for the rest of the Turn too, once those exist — a Warrior who leaps into the middle punishes everything that walks past.
powers.source: 2026-08-21: "Leap. It'll move you two squares with no attacks of opportunity given. Cost 2 stamina. And give you +2 Strength until the end of your activation. And this one goes on a Warrior. And let's remove the one we gave to Priest and Mage, they both don't get one." | 2026-08-21: "isn’t the end of activation the same as the end of this turn? I’m not trying to add one." An Activation is movement plus ONE primary action, so “until the end of your Activation” is exactly the one swing after the leap — and with attacks of opportunity unbuilt, that is behaviourally identical to end of the Turn today. Using the duration that already exists rather than adding a fifth. The two diverge once AoO is built, and end-of-Turn is the more generous reading, which suits a Warrior that just landed in the middle. | 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation — you pick Move, a Flight, or your bonus move, never two. "Only the full movement actions and things like them benefit from the Move stat, so all of these bonus moves do not benefit from the Move stat."

powers.name: Focus
powers.description: Do not move at all. Gain 1 Stamina. It costs no Stamina and there is no cooldown. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat — it moves you zero hexes on purpose. Mages only.
powers.intent: The Mage’s bonus move is to stand still and breathe. It is the cheapest stamina in the game and the price is that you are exactly where you were — a caught caster can Focus, but it will still be caught.
powers.source: 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation — you pick Move, a Flight, or your bonus move, never two. "Only the full movement actions and things like them benefit from the Move stat, so all of these bonus moves do not benefit from the Move stat."

powers.name: Devotion
powers.description: Do not move at all. Lose 1 Stamina Max for the rest of the Battle, and gain 2 Stamina. There is no cooldown. It is a bonus move, so it does NOT add your Movement stat — it moves you zero hexes on purpose. Priests only.
powers.intent: Burn the candle. Two Stamina now against a bar that is one shorter for the rest of the fight, and you may do it again, and again, until there is no bar left. The Priest chooses how much of the end of the battle to spend on the middle of it.
powers.source: 2026-08-21: the BONUS MOVE family. "Mage gets Focus. It actually does zero movement, zero stamina cost. They gain one stamina. Priest gets Devotion. Does zero movement. They lose 1 maximum stamina, and they gain 2 stamina." A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation — you pick Move, a Flight, or your bonus move, never two. "Only the full movement actions and things like them benefit from the Move stat, so all of these bonus moves do not benefit from the Move stat."

powers.name: Flight
powers.description: Movement action. Move up to your Movement, 1 Movement per hex, passing over units and obstructions and taking nothing from the ground on the way — no terrain cost, no trap, no hex status. Where you LAND is a hex like any other.
powers.intent: One click, straight over everything in between.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: flight is a granted movement power, never a standing property. Items that used to say "you have FLIGHT" grant this.

powers.name: Flight (Swift)
powers.description: Movement action. Move up to your Movement + 1, 1 Movement per hex, passing over units and obstructions and taking nothing from the ground on the way. Costs no Stamina.
powers.intent: The good version: a hex further than anyone else, and it costs nothing.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: "give a power move flight cost 0 stamina, moves +1, as a flight." Granted by item.aegis-of-the-fleet.

powers.name: Flight (Labored)
powers.description: Movement action. Move up to your Movement - 1, 1 Movement per hex, passing over units and obstructions and taking nothing from the ground on the way. Costs 2 Stamina.
powers.intent: It gets you over the thing in the way and it charges you for the privilege.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: the weak rung of the flight ladder — labored 2 stamina and Movement -1, standard 1 stamina and full Movement, swift 0 stamina and Movement +1.

powers.name: Karma decay
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every unit in the game carries this: on kill, your Karma drops by 1.
powers.intent: Karma is the only status you spend rather than wait out. It leaves when you take a life.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: "every hero has, on kill, lower Karma by 1."

powers.name: Ground layers
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. There are four ground layers — burning, frost, poisoned and darkness. A layer is PERSISTENT: it carries no number and no clock, and once it is on a hex it stays there. A hex holds exactly ONE layer. Applying a different layer to a hex REPLACES the one already there.
powers.intent: The ground is a state, not a countdown. Frost put out a fire because it took the hex, not because it cancelled anything.
powers.source: 2026-08-20: "Status effects on terrain are just persistent. No turn tracking, just it is burning or it is frost. The only thing that should replace a ground layer effect is if a different one is applied, it replaces the previous one. The ground can only have one effect on it, and that effect stays."

powers.name: Summon order
powers.description: UNIVERSAL RULE, not a power you take. Every summoned unit is given a summon number when it arrives — the first thing summoned is 1, the second is 2, and so on, counted separately for each side. In its own Phase, summoned units activate FIRST, in summon-number order, BEFORE any unit that was already on the field. Summoned heroes go first in the Hero Phase; summoned enemies go first in the Enemy Phase.
powers.intent: A summon that arrives and then waits behind everything else is a summon that did nothing. Going first is most of what you paid for.
powers.source: 2026-08-20. Written ahead of the summoning system itself, which does not exist yet — see engine/COMBAT-SEQUENCE.md #Summoning.

powers.name: Vespers
powers.description: At the end of the priest’s Activation, heal every ally within 4 hexes for HALF the priest’s Spirit — rounded nearest, 0.5 up (ruled 2026-08-25). The four Eve priests share this innate; it is DISTINCT from the Priest Chain’s Benediction, which is an active cast (stamina 2, range 6, 2 + half Spirit). The audit caught the name collision; renamed same day.
powers.source: dictated 2026-08-22 (“heal all heroes within range 4: half of your spirit”), blocked on Law 7 integers, unblocked by the rounding ruling 2026-08-25

powers.name: Pray
powers.description: A bonus move: zero movement, costs 1 Stamina, gain 1 Faith. A bonus move IS your movement for the Activation (2026-08-21 family ruling: Focus/Devotion precedent), and it does not benefit from the Move stat.
powers.intent: Trade your feet for the purse. Faith in combat is the whole point and the whole gap.
powers.source: 2026-08-25, dictated with badge Praying: "gain movement power pray: costs 1 stamina, gain 1 faith". Granted by badge.praying. Faith-in-combat is a recorded capability gap on the badge.

powers.name: Charging Run
powers.description: A full movement action: move up to your Movement +2, and gain +3 Strength until the end of your Activation. Costs 2 Stamina. A full movement action reads the stat — the 2026-08-21 bonus-move ruling, applied in reverse.
powers.intent: Close the distance and arrive angrier.
powers.source: 2026-08-25, dictated with badge Charging: "gain move action: stamina 2, movement +2, gain +3 str until EOA". Granted by badge.charging. NAMED Charging Run because power.charge already exists (the armor-granted one) — name is a proposal, free to change.

items.intent: One point of Immunity makes you substantially immune to the thing. That is the whole item.

items.name: Lumberjack's Axe
items.intent: A working tool that has stopped asking what it is for. The first two-handed axe in the game, and it belongs to a civilian.

attacks.name: Punch
attacks.intent: The attack EVERY PLAYER UNIT has — ruled 2026-08-25, confirming the 2026-08-22 Brawler ruling. Universal: no kit grants it and no row lists it, because a per-row flag would be a second source for one fact. Brawler reads its brawl tag. Damage soft.
attacks.source: authored 2026-08-25 — the universal punch the Brawler ruling required

attacks.name: Cleave
attacks.targets: an adjacent hex and one hex adjacent to both you and it
attacks.source: dictated 2026-08-25 (Lumberjack) — attack 2 hexes; the two-hex sweep shape already exists

statuses.name: Karma
statuses.effect: While you carry Karma: every heal you receive is increased by your Karma, and every point of damage you deal is increased by HALF your Karma, rounded down.
statuses.decay: It does not tick down at End of Phase like the others. Karma is spent by KILLING: every unit in the game has, on kill, lose 1 Karma.
statuses.source: 2026-08-20. The only status that decays on an event rather than on the clock. RE-RULED IDENTICALLY 2026-08-25, verbatim: "Karma increases healing and increases damage by half of the Karma value. So it increases healing to the target that has karma by the amount of karma. And one half of the Karma value is added to all damage. Karma is lost whenever the unit kills another unit. So, every unit, during player attack, if there is a kill, there is a check to see if there is karma, and if there is, it goes down by one."

statuses.name: Slow
statuses.effect: While you carry Slow, your Movement is reduced by your Slow.
statuses.decay: -1 at End of Phase, like Burn, Poison, Bleed, Weak, Stun and Frost.
statuses.source: 2026-08-20: "clean up that movement stuff." Fourteen entries said "the target loses N Movement on its next Turn" — one meaning, two wordings, and the only per-target clock left in the game. It is a status now, so it decays on the same ladder as everything else and nothing has to remember whose next Turn it is.

testCohort.note: Ruled 2026-08-20: the standard engine test party — six heroes, one per class, COPIED from live Codex heroes so they can be tweaked without touching the originals. Clearly differentiated: test- typeIds, (TEST) names, never ships. The engine reads these through the generated pack (mkenginepack.mjs) — nothing hand-typed engine-side. Testing-lane riders travel on the cohort and retire one by one as published sources land; the Sky Pirate's own Cutlass bleed already retires test.ranger.serrated-arrows.
testCohort._movesNote: moves are derived from the class bonusMove in gen/classes.json, ruled 2026-08-21: Warrior Leap, Rogue/Ranger Side Roll, Paladin Sidestep, Mage Focus, Priest Devotion, Civilian/Beast none. Corrected 2026-08-21 - the cohort had been carrying the pre-rebuild assignment where nearly everyone got Sidestep. audit.mjs enforces the match, so restoring the old values will fail the build.
testCohort._copyOfNote: Lucius and Osric were tutorial heroes. The tutorial path was cut 2026-08-21 - its 96 rows were 24 heroes duplicated across their own level art - so they now copy the eve-base heroes that own those pictures. The cohort still covers six classes.

alphaTeam.note: THE ALPHA TEAM, dictated 2026-08-27: "take those heroes and make them the way they are supposed to actually be in content" — the test cohort rebuilt on the real scaffolding. Same stat bodies (copied from testCohort, which copied live heroes 2026-08-20), one hero per class, but armed through kit -> authored items -> authored attack rows instead of the engine's six PROVISIONAL attacks. Test-only statuses translated into the vocabulary: ward->protection, hobble->slow, enfeeble->weak. Punch arrives via universalToAllUnits, never listed. Movement powers are derived from class by the converter. Clearly differentiated: alpha- typeIds, (ALPHA) names, never ships. Arcane Bolt is NOT carried over — the Air Mage's ability is now the Lightning Staff's, as a real item grant.

critChart.note: RULED DATA, NOT A CONTENT KIND (decided 2026-08-27, closing the question parked 2026-08-09). One copy, here; COMBAT-DESIGN.md crit section is the design authority and this block mirrors it. The chart never produces an injury.* badge — battle-only, cleared at battle end; permanence is the Deathbed pipeline alone. Resolution: normal damage always lands; cup.crit-branch flips a coin — heads +50% damage BEFORE Armor/Resist/Protection, tails cup.crit-effect rolls evenly among the rows. One chart for all damage types, fully symmetric. Entry point name fixed in GLOSSARY.md: rollCritEffect. Row keys exist so event-log lines can name their cause (Law 12) — keys, not content ids.
